title: absoluteUrl() accepts protocol-relative paths, enabling off-site canonical/OG URLs (latent open redirect)
detail: absoluteUrl() builds the canonical/OpenGraph URL via new URL(canonicalPath, SITE_URL) without validating that `path` is a same-origin pathname. A value beginning with "//" (e.g. "//evil.com/x") makes new URL resolve to https://evil.com/x, so the page's <link rel=canonical>, og:url, and twitter card would point at an attacker-controlled origin. Today every caller passes a literal internal path, so this is latent; it becomes exploitable the moment `path` is derived from a request param, CMS field, or config merge.

title: String.replace with string replacement interprets $ patterns — latent script-injection/corruption in generated inline <script>

title: Custom response headers (Content-Type, Cache-Control) are silently discarded under static export

title: Ingest handler blocks on upstream PostHog round trip before responding
detail: forwardToPostHog awaits the fetch() to PostHog (/capture/) before returning a response to the caller. Every analytics beacon pays the full third-party RTT (typically 100–500ms+, worse during PostHog incidents), holding the Worker request open, increasing wall-clock/CPU-billable time, and delaying or timing out client-side sendBeacon/fetch keepalive calls. For a fire-and-forget ingest endpoint this upstream call should be detached from the response path.
fix: Change the export to `async fetch(request, env, ctx)` and move the upstream POST behind `ctx.waitUntil(...)`: build the body, kick off `const p = fetch(`${host}/capture/`, {...})` inside `ctx.waitUntil(p.catch(() => {}))`, and immediately return `json({ ok: true }, { status: 202, headers: corsHeaders(request, env) })`. Accept losing the mirrored upstream status in the response (standard for analytics ingestion); optionally log failures inside the waitUntil callback.
verify_reason: Evidence shows the handler awaits the PostHog /capture/ fetch before returning, so every ingest request blocks on full third-party RTT and mirrors upstream status — a known anti-pattern for fire-and-forget analytics ingestion on Workers. The proposed ctx.waitUntil() fix is idiomatic and correct. Minor overstatement: Workers bill CPU time, not I/O wait, so 'CPU-billable time' impact is negligible, but the latency/resource-holding and client keepalive-delay concerns are real.

title: crypto.randomUUID() fallback fragments every event into its own person
detail: When no distinct_id/anonymous_id is supplied, each event receives a fresh UUID, so PostHog records a brand-new person per event. This inflates monthly tracked users (direct billing impact on PostHog) and destroys funnel/retention coherence for any client integration that forgets to send an ID.
evidence: payload.distinct_id || payload.anonymous_id || clientIp(request) || crypto.randomUUID();
fix: Require anonymous_id (drop the event with a 400 if absent), and generate the anonymous_id once client-side (localStorage/cookie) so it persists across events; remove the randomUUID fallback entirely.
